paragraphs: (Hyman gives the biblical name Armoni son of Saul and cites II Samuel 21:18.) He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan, chapter 3, halakhah 5, folio 12b: Rabbi Mana instructed him (concerning mourning): “Since you are the head of the family,” etc.

notes.text: The supplied biblical locator is II Samuel 21:18; Armoni son of Saul appears in the Miqra digital II Samuel 21:8, added here alongside the supplied reference. The supplied אכילות means “meals,” but the Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5 passage explicitly concerns counting mourning days, supporting the contextual reading אבילות, “mourning.” This establishes the topic, not which letters appeared on Hyman’s printed page; that question remains open.

The inspected printing of Hyman (vol. I, p. 243) reads אבילות, “mourning,” where the supplied Hebrew has אכילות, “meals.” In the Jerusalem Talmud passage, Rabbi Mana tells Rabbi Armaniyya to count the days himself as head of the family. Guggenheimer’s English gives “Jacob in Armenia,” incorporating an addition from witness A. Hyman’s biblical cross-reference is printed as II Samuel 21:18. Armoni son of Saul is named at 21:8, and the biblical aside describes a separate context.
